description:
ANANTA is a team passionate about Artificial Intelligence, space exploration, and humanity’s future beyond Earth. We aim to combine AI, data science, and scientific innovation to solve challenges in planetary exploration and sustainable extraterrestrial habitats. Inspired by the idea of infinity, we believe the possibilities of discovery are limitless.

ANANTA — Intelligence Beyond Earth.
summary:
ARES-NAV (Adaptive Route & Environment Survival Navigation) is an integrated Martian planetary intelligence, extra-vehicular activity (EVA) route-planning, and habitat-siting web platform built on real NASA datasets. Addressing the Interplanetary Survival Guide challenge, ARES-NAV fuses MGS MOLA laser altimetry, MRO CTX/HiRISE imagery, CRISM spectral mineralogy, Curiosity RAD radiation archives, Perseverance MEDA and Curiosity REMS weather telemetry, and NAIF SPICE orbital ephemerides across 10 candidate Martian landing sectors.

Future crewed Mars expeditions face up to 22.3-minute one-way light-time communication delays, eliminating real-time dependency on Earth Mission Control during emergencies. ARES-NAV empowers astronauts and mission planners with autonomous, physics-based decision support: an 8-mode anisotropic A* pathfinder with Pandolf 0.38g bioenergetic consumable tracking (O2, battery, Point-of-No-Return alerts), Solar Particle Event (SPE) emergency shelter routing, 3D UHF line-of-sight relay placement, and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) basecamp siting. Dual Beginner/Expert modes make complex planetary engineering accessible to both scientists and students.
details:
What It Does & How It Works ARES-NAV (Adaptive Route & Environment Survival Navigation) transforms fragmented NASA orbital and in-situ archives into an interactive 2D/3D tactical mission control platform across 10 Martian exploration sectors (Jezero Crater, Melas Chasma, Arcadia Planitia, Gale Crater, Olympus Mons, NE Syrtis Major, Mawrth Vallis, Hellas Planitia, Gusev Crater, and Elysium Planitia).

Core capabilities include:

  • Dual 2D GIS & 3D Topographic Hologram Engine: Renders 9 scientific and tactical layers—Composite Survival Map, MOLA Elevation DEM, Geodesic Slope (NASA-STD-3001 compliance), HiRISE Sub-Meter Boulder Density, CRISM Mineralogy, SHARAD Subsurface H2​O Ice, UHF Communications Line-of-Sight, Dynamic Multi-Hazard Risk Heatmap, and Habitat Suitability.
  • Explainable Multi-Objective EVA Route Optimization: Uses an anisotropic A∗ pathfinder across 8 operational modes (Shortest, Fastest, Safest, Lowest Resource, Min Radiation, Comm-Aware, Science, Balanced) plus an SPE Solar Storm Emergency Abort router that computes the fastest escape trajectory to habitat airlocks or natural terrain overhangs during coronal mass ejections.
  • Bioenergetic Consumables & Point-of-No-Return (PNR) Checker: Applies the Pandolf metabolic equation adapted for Martian gravity (0.38g0.38g0.38g) to track Portable Life Support System (PLSS) O2 draw (580 L), battery drain (1850 Wh), and turnaround thresholds (FEASIBLE / MARGINAL / CRITICAL).
  • 3D UHF Link Budget & Autonomous Relay Placement: Ray-marches NASA Proximity-1 (401.58 MHz) radio propagation with knife-edge diffraction and uses a greedy set-cover optimizer to position astronaut-deployable tripod relays ([R-α], [R-β]) that eliminate communication dead zones.
  • NAIF SPICE Ephemeris & In-Situ Weather Engine: Computes real-time areocentric solar longitude (Ls​), true local solar time (LT), topocentric solar insolation, and astronomical One-Way Light Time (OWLT=d/c), paired with calibrated Perseverance MEDA and Curiosity REMS weather observations and Ingenuity-class scout drone flight envelope checks.
  • MCDA / Saaty AHP Habitat & Infrastructure Triad Siting: Evaluates 80×8080 sector grids using a verified 6×66 Analytic Hierarchy Process matrix to site the primary Habitat Basecamp, Solar Array Farm, and Kilo power Fission Reactor (≥500 m crew radiation standoff) while enforcing an 800 m–2000 m Human Landing System (HLS) rocket plume blast exclusion buffer.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Autonomous Crew Survival Under Latency: With Earth–Mars one-way light time ranging from 3.1 to 22.3 minutes, astronauts cannot wait for Houston during a suit leak or solar storm. ARES-NAV provides instantaneous local route recalculation, consumable reserve auditing, and emergency shelter selection.
  • Scientific Transparency & Data Provenance: Every layer and telemetry stream carries an explicit provenance badge (VERIFIED, PARTIAL, CALCULATED_CALIBRATED, or ANALYTICAL_HYDROSTATIC_MODEL) and uncertainty budget, preventing black-box hallucinations in safety-critical mission planning.
  • Public & Educational Accessibility: Features a 1-click Beginner / Expert Mode toggle, a 9-step interactive onboarding walkthrough, a 13-term Mars Science Knowledge Centre, and a 5-stage Custom Dataset Upload wizard (CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, PNG/JPG) that actively updates A∗A^*A∗ hazard circumvention.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Backend: Python 3.10+, Standard Library http.server REST API (nasa/server.py), spiceypy (NASA NAIF SPICE kernel evaluation with calibrated Keplerian fallback), and Pillow (orbital raster and Sobel/Laplacian boulder variance processing).
  • Frontend: Vanilla ES6 JavaScript modules, HTML5 2D Canvas & custom 3D painter's-algorithm projection engine (nasa/static/app.js), and CSS3 tactical HUD interface—built with zero heavy frontend frameworks for fast, dependency-free execution.
  • NASA Data & Kernels: NASA Mars Trek WMTS (MGS MOLA, MRO CTX), PDS Orbital Data Explorer (MRO HiRISE, MRO CRISM), PDS PPI (MSL Curiosity RAD dosimetry), PDS Atmospheres (Mars 2020 MEDA, MSL REMS), and JPL NAIF SPICE kernels (de440s.bsp, mar099s.bsp, pck00010.tpc, naif0012.tls).

How Our Project Is Creative & Factors Considered

  • Physics-First Engineering Rigor: Rather than treating Mars as a flat 2D game map, our team modeled directional slope penalties, 0.38g human metabolic expenditure, solid-angle horizon sky-view masking versus bulk regolith neutron spallation, and HLS plume ejecta exclusion zones.
  • Strict Separation of Physical vs. Operational Realities: We explicitly separate astronomical light-time latency (OWLTOWLTOWLT) from Deep Space Network (DSN) scheduling buffers, and assign a strict 100% risk penalty to unmapped (NaN) terrain cells so autonomous routes never cut through unverified ground.
